text: Hear this word that I raise over you as a lament, house of Israel:
Fallen is the virgin Israel, never to rise again; abandoned on her own soil, with no one to lift her up.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: The city that marches out a thousand strong will have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: Seek me and live!
Do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, do not journey to Beersheba. For Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
Seek the LORD and live, or he will break out like fire against the house of Joseph—it will devour, and there will be no one at Bethel to put it out.
You who turn justice into bitterness and throw righteousness to the ground!

He it is who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens the day into night. He summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is his name.

versions.text: He made the Pleiades and Orion; he turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night. He summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is his name.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses a chain of participles (עֹשֵׂה, הֹפֵךְ, הַקּוֹרֵא) describing God's timeless character in hymnic style, not a single past act. Rendering the first as a simple past tense ("He made") breaks the doxological pattern; a relative/participial chain keeps the hymn's rhythm and unity for oral reading.

text: He brings ruin on the strong, and destruction comes upon the fortress.
They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they despise the one who speaks with integrity.

versions.text: They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they despise the one who speaks the truth.
versions.explanation: תָּמִים denotes wholeness or integrity rather than factual truth specifically; "speaks with integrity" or "speaks honestly" is closer to the Hebrew and matches the legal-court setting of the city gate.

text: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and extort grain from them, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted lovely vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
For I know how many your transgressions are, how great your sins: you oppress the righteous, you take bribes, and you turn the needy away in the gate.
Therefore the prudent keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good, not evil, that you may live. Then the LORD, the God of hosts, will be with you, just as you claim.
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps then the LORD, the God of hosts, will show mercy to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the Lord, says: In every public square there will be wailing, and in every street they will cry, "Alas! Alas!" They will call the farmers to mourning and the singers of dirges to lamentation.
There will be wailing in every vineyard, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.
Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD! What will that day be for you? It will be darkness, not light.
It will be as when a man flees from a lion, only to meet a bear; or he comes home, rests his hand against the wall, and a snake bites him.
Will not the day of the LORD be darkness and not light, gloom without a ray of brightness?
I hate, I despise your festivals; I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
Even if you bring me burnt offerings, I will not accept them; your grain offerings give me no pleasure, and I will not look at the fellowship offerings of your fattened cattle.
Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps.
But let justice roll on like water, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings those forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
Yet you carried Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.

versions.text: No—you carried Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star-god you made for yourselves.
versions.explanation: The introductory "No—" is an interpretive addition not present in the Hebrew (which simply begins with the connective waw); "Yet" preserves the connection to the rhetorical question of v. 25 without inserting an answer. Also, כּוֹכַב אֱלֹהֵיכֶם is literally "the star of your god," and a footnote noting that Sikkuth and Kiyyun are likely names of Mesopotamian astral deities would help the reader.

text: So I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD, whose name is the God of hosts.
